name: Agabus
description: Man living at the time of the New Testament

points: And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world. A great dearth is what you call a famine.

note.label: Integrated but Divided: What Did We Lose?

points: Agabus signified by the spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world, which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar. Understand that Caligula was Caesar when this was prophesied; Claudius came into power four or five years later, and that is when the famine hit, around AD 45 to 46. This is why, when we tell you to prepare, black people say it did not happen this year or next, so it is not going to happen. This did not occur for five years. Just listen closely when we tell you things.

In those days prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch, and one named Agabus signified by the Spirit that there would be a great dearth throughout all the world, which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar. This famine is historically documented; Elliott's commentary notes the frequent famines of Claudius's reign, and Josephus records a famine affecting Judea and Syria under the procurator Cuspius Fadus around AD 45, when Queen Helena of Adiabene sent supplies of corn and figs, again giving validity to the Bible as an accurate history book.
